subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Show that at any point (x, y) on the curve y = b e^(x/a): (i) the length of the subtangent is constant, and (ii) the length of the subnormal is y²/a.

mark_split.label: Differentiate and write dy/dx in terms of y

recall_prompt: Say how you would show both parts — say what dy/dx works out to in terms of y, then the two formulas you divide and multiply with.

steps.label: Differentiate and write dy/dx in terms of y
steps.margin_note: First mark. Writing dy/dx as y/a rather than as (b/a)eˣ⁄ᵃ is the move that makes both parts one line each. Both parts of the question are about y, not about x.
lines: Differentiate with respect to x. The exponent x/a differentiates to 1/a:

recall.must_convey: That dy/dx = (b/a)eˣ⁄ᵃ, and since b eˣ⁄ᵃ is y itself, dy/dx = y/a.
accept: differentiate and the chain rule gives one by a
b e power x by a is y itself so dy by dx is y by a
replace the exponential by y
b e power x by a ante y ye kabatti dy by dx equals y by a
the derivative is the curve divided by a
dy by dx equals y over a
heard_as: b e power x by a

steps.why: An exponential differentiates to a constant times itself, so dy/dx can be written in terms of y with no exponential left. Both parts asked for are stated in y, so this form is the one that answers them directly.
common_mistakes: Writing dy/dx = b eˣ⁄ᵃ and omitting the 1/a from the chain rule.
Writing dy/dx = ay instead of y/a, inverting the constant.
Differentiating b as well, when b is a constant.
steps.memory_tip: An exponential is its own derivative up to a constant. For b eˣ⁄ᵃ that constant is 1/a, so dy/dx is y/a.

steps.label: State the two lengths
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Both definitions are worth writing down before either is used — the examiner gives the mark for the correct pair, and stating them stops the two being swapped.
lines: At a point (x, y) on a curve, with m = dy/dx:
length of the subnormal = y · m

recall.must_convey: That subtangent = y/m and subnormal = ym.
accept: the subtangent is y divided by the slope
the subnormal is y times the slope
subtangent is y by m and subnormal is y m
subtangent ante y by m, subnormal ante y into m
one divides by the slope and the other multiplies
state both definitions before substituting

steps.why: The two lengths differ only in whether m divides or multiplies, so they are easy to swap under exam pressure. Writing both down first makes the choice in each part deliberate.
common_mistakes: Writing the subtangent as ym and the subnormal as y/m, the two exchanged.
Using the length of the tangent y√(1 + m²)/m in place of the subtangent.
Substituting numbers before either definition is stated, so no method mark is available.
steps.memory_tip: Both start from y. The subtangent divides by the slope, the subnormal multiplies by it.

steps.label: (i) The subtangent is constant
steps.margin_note: Third mark. y cancels completely, which is what makes the length constant. Say so in words — a proof of "constant" is not finished until the absence of x and y is stated.
lines: a is a fixed number, and no x or y is left in the result.
∴ the length of the subtangent is a, the same at every point of the curve.

recall.must_convey: That y/m = y ÷ (y/a) = a, so the subtangent is the constant a.
accept: divide y by y over a
the y cancels and only a is left
the subtangent is a which is a constant
y cancel ayipoyi a matrame migulutundi
it does not depend on the point
the length of the subtangent is the constant a

steps.why: Dividing by a fraction is multiplying by its reciprocal, so y ÷ (y/a) becomes y × a/y and the y's cancel. The result contains only the given constant a, which is exactly what "constant" means here.
common_mistakes: Writing y ÷ (y/a) as y²/a, multiplying instead of dividing.
Getting 1/a by cancelling the a as well.
Stopping at the value a without saying that it does not depend on the point.
steps.memory_tip: Dividing by y/a is the same as multiplying by a/y. The two y's then cancel and a survives alone.

steps.label: (ii) The subnormal is y²/a
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. Same m, the other operation. The subnormal does depend on the point, so unlike part (i) it is not constant — do not claim it is.
lines: Length of the subnormal = y · m

lines.text: ∴ (i) subtangent = a, a constant     (ii) subnormal = y²/a

accept: multiply y by y over a
the subnormal is y squared by a
y into y by a gives y square by a
y ni y by a tho multiply cheste y square by a
this one changes from point to point
the subnormal is not constant

steps.why: The same slope y/a is used, multiplied this time instead of divided. y stays in the answer, so the subnormal grows as the curve rises — only the subtangent is constant on this curve.
common_mistakes: Writing the subnormal as a as well, copying the answer to part (i).
Writing y²a instead of y²/a, multiplying by a rather than dividing.
Saying the subnormal is also constant, when it still contains y.
steps.memory_tip: Part (i) divides, part (ii) multiplies, and the slope y/a is the same in both. One answer keeps y, the other loses it.
